edits.new:
Read this social-media post as a whole and build a hierarchy of its subjects, like a book's subject index organized into broad headings and increasingly specific subheadings.

Include general subjects, more specific subjects, and particular instances. Place each specific subject beneath a broader one it refines. Give every heading and subheading its own entry; subjects may overlap or appear in multiple branches.

Include subjects conveyed literally, nonliterally, or rhetorically by individual parts, multiple parts together, or the post as a whole, even when no phrase names them. Index individual subjects as well as the combinations expressed by the passage.

Ground every entry in the complete post, excluding URLs. General knowledge may clarify language, identify referents, and recognize subjects, but every entity, modifier, action, and relationship in an entry must be stated or reasonably implied by the post.

Interpret names, labels, and hashtags by what they refer to; their component words alone do not establish a literal description. For an unresolved named subject, retain its name. Exclude labels, credits, or identifiers used merely to present the content.

If ambiguity remains after understanding the complete post, give each supported interpretation its own directly stated subject, without uncertainty qualifiers. Co-mention or statement order alone does not establish relationships. Do not add commentary about plausibility or what is unclear or unstated.

For numbers in subject text, preserve what they refer to; any count or measurement interpretation and units must be supported by the post. Include calculated results only if explicitly stated.

Use section-style numbering (`1`, `1.1`, `1.1.1`), listing each heading before its subheadings. Return an object for each entry with `number`, then `context`, then `subject`.

In `context`, identify the subject and the source context establishing its meaning. Resolve references to the most specific descriptions supported by the complete post.

In `subject`, give a standalone heading understandable without the post, its `context`, or other entries. It may name a subject without retelling what the post says about it. Preserve the entry's meaning, negation, and relationships. For comparison entries, name both sides when provided. Make the wording concise.
edits.old:
Read this social-media post as a whole and build a hierarchy of its subjects, like a book's subject index organized into broad headings and increasingly specific subheadings.

Include both the general subjects represented by the post and the more specific subjects and particular instances it discusses. Place each more specific subject beneath a broader subject it refines. Give every heading and subheading its own entry. Subjects may overlap or appear in more than one branch.

Include subjects the post conveys literally, nonliterally, or rhetorically, whether through the whole post, an individual part, or multiple parts together, even when no single phrase names the subject. When a passage concerns several subjects together, index those subjects individually as well as the combinations expressed by the passage.

Use the complete post, excluding URLs, as evidence for every subject. Use general knowledge only to interpret language and resolve references. Every entity, modifier, action, and relationship in an entry must be stated or reasonably implied by that text.

Interpret names and labels, including hashtags, by what they refer to in the post. Their component words alone do not establish a literal description of that referent. When a subject is identified by name but its meaning cannot be resolved, retain its name rather than inventing a descriptive expansion.

Index only subjects represented by the post. Do not add your own commentary about a subject's plausibility or about what the post leaves unclear or unstated. Subjects concern the communicated content, not labels, credits or identifiers used merely to present it. For numbers included in the subject text, preserve what they refer to; their role as a count or measurement and any units must be supported by the text. Return a calculated result only when the result itself is explicitly stated in the post.

When a specific expression or relationship remains ambiguous after reading the complete post, represent each supported interpretation as a separate subject. State each interpretation directly as a subject, without uncertainty qualifiers. The order or proximity of separate statements does not itself establish a relationship between them. Co-mention does not by itself establish participation or causation.

Use section-style numbering such as `1`, `1.1`, and `1.1.1` to show the hierarchy, listing each heading before its subheadings.

Return an object for each heading or subheading, with `number`, then `context`, then `subject`. In `context`, identify the subject this entry names and the source context needed to establish its intended meaning. Resolve context-dependent references to the most specific descriptions of those references supported by the complete post. In `subject`, give the standalone subject heading or subheading.

Each `subject` must be understandable without the post, its `context` field, or other entries. This means making the subject's identity and meaning clear, not reproducing every action, circumstance, or claim surrounding it. An entry can name a subject without restating what the post says about that subject. When an entry names a comparison, include both sides if the post provides them. Preserve the meaning, negation, and relationships expressed by the entry. Make its wording concise.
